Work requires a bachelor's degree in botany, biology, zoology, psychology or other directly related scientific field.
Work requires four years of research experience. A related master's degree may offset required years of experience on a 1:1 basis, e.g., a two year master's degree in lieu of two years of experience. OR AN EQUIVALENT COMBINATION OF RELEVANT EDUCATION AND/OR EXPERIENCE

Preferred Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in biological science or related field.
Strong background in laboratory techniques including experience with cell culture, cell based neutralization assays and infectious materials including infectious influenza virus is a plus.
Work requires four years of research experience. A related master's degree may offset required years of experience on a 1:1 basis, e.g., a two year master's degree in lieu of two years of experience, or equivalent combination of relevant education and research experience.
Must be able to manage multiple and rapidly changing priorities and have the ability to quickly learn new skills.
Must be detail-oriented and well organized with strong communication skills and the ability to work in a fast-paced interactive team environment.

Other Requirements

This position is onsite. The work is performed on-site or at a designated assignment location.

Be Bold.

Coordinate with Laboratory Study Managers on clinical study management lifecycle duties including development of cumulative specimen lists, tracking testing status, data quality control and documentation assembly, and data visualization. Contribute to QA documentation, corrective actions, and continuous improvement efforts by identifying nonconformances and recommending operational enhancements. Develop and refine data tracking tools and workflows to improve efficiency, accuracy, and audit readiness.
Serve as laboratory’s lead technical and laboratory systems trainer for new hires and new processes for existing staff. Work with laboratory management and quality team to ensure compliance, documentation and best practices.
Serve as lead laboratory staff for laboratory’s HIV and COVID-19 clinical testing programs including additional GCLP documentation, data quality control, assay tracking and reporting guidelines. Serve as subject matter expert for clinical testing. Serve as a lead assay representative for both internal and external audits of laboratory technical components.
Provision of rapid assay qualification/validation experiment, special technical projects as needed and coordination across teams for deployment of updated processes and technologies.
Co-direct clinical specimen management for Laboratory’s support of HIV and COVID-19 vaccine clinical trials. Coordinate with Laboratory Program Team and manage clinical specimen cumulative receipt and testing lists for assay planning and timeline development. Provide as training and support to other staff for clinical specimen access, database entry and resolution of issues.
Develop and implement process improvement projects specific to clinical study laboratory operations. Oversee application of new processes and workflows to ensure systems compliance, support enhanced lab operations, improve user interfaces, improve stakeholder communication and documentation, and ensure traceability and compliance.
Assessment of neutralizing antibody responses in various cell lines in support of pre-clinical and clinical HIV-1 and COVID-19 vaccine development. Performance of more advanced research activities and projects. Conduct all experiments with complete adherence to Good Clinical Laboratory Practices (GCLP) guidelines.
Data analysis with adherence to quality control pass/fail criteria. Report results in an accurate and timely manner to Laboratory Directors and Study Directors. Review results for use in planning new experiments/analyses. Provision of rapid data quality control for other team members and Study Manager level assessments.
Contribute to the daily laboratory effort to adhere to GCLP guidelines. Provide timely and critical review of SOPs as requested. Adhere to all required safety, data integrity and policy protocols to protect staff, data integrity and others.

As a Project Manager, you will be responsible for effectively managing commercial construction projects in the low-slope roofing category including sheet metal installation and masonry restoration (as needed) by the scope of the contract.

:

Assist leadership team in identifying excellent and poor performance in the field

Possess high-level written and verbal communication skill

new_jobs.title: Physical Security Project Manager
new_jobs.description:
WHO WE ARE

ZBeta is a world-class physical security design, consulting, and managed services firm that partners with some of the most dynamic, high-profile organizations and individuals in the world. We leverage a Data Driven, Technology Led, Human Centered approach in order to help our clients architect and engineer superior physical security solutions, implement them seamlessly, and operate them at peak efficiency. ZBeta prides itself on its level of technical expertise but remains independent and product-agnostic. Our highly experienced team brings decades of security expertise, diverse organizational perspectives, and proven best practices to every project and customer. It is our meticulous attention to detail, and our ability to deliver at scale that positions us to deliver an exceptional customer experience.

Our primary goal is to redefine the standards of professional security, equipping our clients with innovative tools to master today’s challenges and fortify against tomorrow's risks. By consistently delivering exceptional solutions and pioneering advancements in the security field, we can exceed expectations and set new standards of excellence in pursuing our vision.

Find out more about us here .

WHO YOU ARE

You are a forward-thinking strategic partner with a passion for enhancing security measures and fostering community resilience. You excel in fast-paced settings where your leadership abilities can catalyze meaningful transformation. You thrive in a workplace culture that is:
Innovative
Strives for Excellence
Reliable
Detail Oriented
Adaptable
Highly Organized
Client Obsessed
Curious
Resilient

Does this sound like you? If so, join us in our mission to redefine security standards and make a lasting difference in our community.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

As a Physical Security
Project Manager
, you will support security design and installation projects throughout the North Coast. The Project Manager is responsible for managing all aspects of the project from initial engagement through project completion, including managing multiple projects and scopes of work.

You are a resourceful, knowledgeable, and self-motivated security professional who thrives in a collaborative and supportive environment.

CORE COMPETENCIES

Growth Minded:
Strong self-awareness of strengths and development areas with a curiosity and appetite for change and innovation
Data-Driven:
Strong analytical skills with critical thinking driven by data
Collaborative
: Ability to solicit and understand multiple perspectives
Evaluative:
Ability to evaluate outputs rigorously to ensure consistent excellence in delivery
Strategic Thinker:
Ability to think proactively about the future of the business and relate current business activities to desired outcomes

POSITION RESPONSIBILITIES

The essential duties and responsibilities include, but are not limited to the following:

Project Management

Identify project schedule, scope parameters, and oversee security design and implementation per client design requirements and standards.
Manage early project initiation activities and develop project security scope, schedule, critical deliverables, and requirements.
Manage scheduling, status, and tracking of critical project tasks, issues, and deliverables.
Prepare, issue, and manage Request for Proposal (RFP) documents for security systems installation scope.
Evaluate RFP responses and prepare evaluation reports, to include evaluation criteria, scoring, and recommendation details.

Design

Perform security site evaluations of potential client properties and review proposed design concepts.
Apply client system design standards to in-progress site design, collaborate with client owner and user group stakeholders to define use cases and verify functional requirements, and produce a security functional specification for the project.
Review all security system design documentation for compliance with published security requirements, technical standards, and installation standards.
Redline documentation with corrections and log issues, as required.

Client Relationship

Accountable for keeping clients informed of project status, including budget, schedule, issues, etc., and managing the client's expectations around the project design through individual and project team member communication.

Collaborate

Serve as a primary security point of contact for project teams and stakeholders.
Attend regular project design, project management, Owner/Architect/Contractor (OAC), and construction meetings.
Manage site activation activities for physical security amongst project parties and stakeholders to drive schedule, quality, and cost.
Coordinate with ZBeta design resources to develop the complete scope of work documents for security systems procurement and installation.

Documentation

Produce project status and issues reports and meet with client stakeholders weekly to review and resolve high-priority project issues.
Log all instances of issue resolutions that constitute exceptions to the published client security requirements to facilitate effective requirements exceptions reporting and/or requirement document updates.

Quality Control

Conduct on-site inspections during construction and installation and final acceptance testing of completed systems installation.
Manage project lessons learned, site metrics evaluation, and contractor performance evaluations.
Review all security system design documentation produced by the system designer for compliance with published security requirements, technical standards, and installation standards.
Oversee the delivery of all shop drawings and close-out documentation required from the integrator/contractor.

WHAT YOU'LL NEED

Experience:
3+ years of project management experience, preferably in consulting with external clients on program development initiatives, and aggressively scheduled design and delivery projects
Education:
Bachelor’s degree or equivalent work experience
Knowledge:

Working familiarity with low-voltage and physical security technology and design concepts

Skills:

Highly proficient in the use of Microsoft Office software
Proficiency in Studio and Bluebeam is a plus
Proficiency in project management tools, such as MS Project, SharePoint, and QuickBase

Abilities

Demonstrated excellence in communicating and presenting complex information to technical and non-technical stakeholders, both verbally and in written form
Demonstrated ability to identify critical path activities, prioritize tasks and deliverables, and realize consistent progress

WHAT WE OFFER

Competitive salary based on job-related skills, experience, and qualifications
ZBeta is a remote-first company with a distributed team. This role is open to individuals based in the United States.
Our excellent benefits package includes 100% paid premiums on health, dental, vision, and life insurance, a 401k retirement plan, and significant work schedule and workplace flexibility.
Diverse and supportive culture

WHAT'S IMPORTANT TO KNOW

We are open to hiring candidates to work out of the North Coast (Santa Rosa, Sonoma, Napa)
This position is an embedded position and will work directly with our client
This position requires the ability to travel up to 50%
This position is not eligible for visa sponsorship
Candidates must be able to meet client and/or government security screening requirements for the role
The successful completion of a background check is required upon hire and every two years thereafter

We look forward to connecting with individuals who are passionate about our mission and can bring diverse contributions to our team — not just those who check all the boxes.

We are committed to creating a supportive, encouraging environment where everyone can fully express their diverse perspectives, showcase their talents, and grow their knowledge, skills, and abilities.

The base pay offered will depend on factors, including but not limited to job-related knowledge, skills, experience, and internal equity. At ZBeta, new hires are rarely placed at the top of the pay range; compensation is determined by the specific circumstances of each position and candidate.

A note to third-party recruiters - we do not accept unsolicited agency resumes, and we are not responsible for any fees related to unsolicited resumes.

Reliable

Highly Organized

Curious

Manage project lessons learned, site metrics evaluation, and contractor performance evaluations.

Description

Amazon is looking for a Technical Program Manager to coordinate security programs, campaigns, and events while also serving as a hands-on builder for smaller-scoped projects using AI tools. You will work within a focused engineering team of network and software engineers that serves its business unit's specific needs directly, rather than building broad, one-size-fits-all solutions. In this role, you will manage program schedules, mitigate risks, and drive cross-team alignment on initiatives such as product migrations. You will also take single-threaded ownership of select builds when the scope calls for it. If you are a collaborative and resourceful program manager who wants to combine coordination with real building, we want to hear from you.

Key job responsibilities

Coordinate security-focused actions, programs, and campaigns end to end — defining goals, building schedules, tracking milestones, mitigating risks, and driving timely decisions to keep efforts on track.
Take hands-on ownership of smaller-scoped builds using AI tools when a project is sized for a single-threaded owner, delivering working solutions directly.
Partner with network and software engineering teams to understand technical requirements, system dependencies, and architecture trade-offs so that solutions meet performance and maintainability standards.
Drive cross-team alignment on org-wide initiatives such as product migrations by owning program communication, resolving conflicting priorities, and escalating blockers appropriately.
Identify opportunities to streamline processes and improve operational efficiency, applying methodologies such as Agile or Lean to reduce delivery risk.

A day in the life

You start your morning reviewing security campaign dashboards and triaging new risks or blockers. By mid-morning, you are leading a cross-team sync to align engineering priorities and confirm delivery commitments for an ongoing product migration. After lunch, you switch context to a smaller build you own directly — prototyping a solution with AI tooling and iterating on feedback from your engineering partners. Later, you draft a status update for leadership that covers progress, open risks, and next steps across your programs.

We are a focused engineering team of network and software engineers that serves our business unit's specialized needs directly. Rather than building broad tools for every use case, we deliver targeted solutions that address the specific challenges our partners face. You will work alongside engineers and stakeholders who value clear communication, practical problem-solving, and getting the right things shipped. Experience working directly with security and engineering teams

new_jobs.title: Power & Hydrogen Program Manager, Power & Hydrogen Solutions, GESA
new_jobs.description:
Description

An execution-focused project/program manager responsible for the hands-on coordination and completion of power capacity and hydrogen fuel cell projects across the Amazon fulfillment network. This is a delivery role with a strong bias for action: the PM owns the details, gets into the field, and drives projects from feasibility through commissioning and handover. Oversees multiple concurrent projects spanning temporary and permanent power deployment (utility upgrades, generator installations, switchgear deployments, and air permitting) as well as hydrogen fuel cell execution — including decommissioning of existing assets, launch of new hydrogen infrastructure and fuel cells per Amazon standards and processes, and conversions of existing sites. Sets deadlines, assigns responsibilities, and personally tracks and unblocks progress. Prepares reports for upper management regarding the status of all projects.

Requires a bachelor's degree and at least 4 years of project management experience in power infrastructure, electrical systems, hydrogen/fuel cell systems, or a related area. The ideal candidate is a hands-on, detail-oriented operator who thrives in ambiguity, dives deep into technical and schedule details, and acts with urgency rather than waiting for direction. Must be familiar with a variety of the field's concepts, practices, and procedures across both power and hydrogen domains. Relies on sound judgment to plan and accomplish goals, and is comfortable rolling up sleeves — walking the site, reading the drawings, chasing the long-lead order, and closing out the punch list. Leads and directs the work of contractors, vendors, and cross-functional teams. A wide degree of creativity and latitude is expected to solve complex energy infrastructure challenges across diverse site conditions and regulatory environments. Typically reports to a manager or head of a unit/department.

Key job responsibilities

Project Management & Bias for Action

Own delivery end to end and act with urgency — move projects forward every day rather than waiting for direction or escalation
Get into the details: read the drawings, interrogate the schedule, understand the single-line and the hydrogen P&ID, and verify the numbers personally
Be hands-on and in the field — walk the site, attend installation and commissioning activities, and verify work directly rather than relying solely on status reports
Build and maintain the plan of record: detailed schedules, critical-path analysis, dependencies, risks, and clear owners and dates
Proactively identify blockers and drive them to closure; dive deep on root cause and remove obstacles for contractors and cross-functional teams
Run a tight operating rhythm — stand-ups, weekly reviews, and crisp written updates that make status and risks unambiguous
Make decisions with incomplete information, bias toward action, and course-correct quickly as new data emerges

Program Coordination & Oversight

Responsible for the coordination and completion of multiple simultaneous power and hydrogen execution projects across U.S. sites
Oversee all aspects of the execution program from feasibility through commissioning and handover
Set deadlines, assign responsibilities, and monitor and summarize the progress of all projects
Prepare reports for upper management regarding program status, including monthly flash updates and executive summaries
Lead and direct the work of contractors, vendors, consultants, and cross-functional teams
Perform a variety of tasks ranging from technical design review to stakeholder management to regulatory coordination

Amazon Standards, Specifications & Quality Assurance

Follow and verify that Amazon standards, specifications, and processes are met across all power and hydrogen infrastructure installations
Ensure electrical equipment, switchgear, generators, fuel cells, hydrogen storage/dispensing systems, and associated systems comply with Amazon technical standards and design requirements
Conduct quality reviews at each project phase to validate adherence to Amazon specifications before progressing to the next milestone
Verify vendor deliverables, shop drawings, and equipment submittals meet Amazon engineering standards
Coordinate with Amazon internal engineering teams to resolve specification questions and obtain approvals
Document and track any deviations from Amazon specifications, securing proper waivers or corrective actions (e.g., Supplier Corrective Action Reports / SCARs)

Power Capacity Execution

Drive execution of temporary and permanent power deployment projects — utility upgrades, generator installations, switchgear deployments, and service upgrades
Oversee deployment of temporary and permanent natural gas and diesel generator systems (1–5MW scale), including rental genset mobilization and conversion to permanent power
Manage utility coordination including transformer upgrades, switchgear installations, and service upgrades with utility companies
Own the end-to-end switchgear (SWGR) procurement process: specification development, vendor selection, purchase order issuance, and delivery tracking
Track SWGR lead times (typically 10–26 weeks) across all sites and ensure orders are placed to meet project timelines; monitor factory acceptance testing (FAT) and coordinate site delivery logistics
Review and validate electrical designs, single-line diagrams, load calculations, and power distribution configurations
Ensure compliance with NEC, NFPA, and local electrical codes

Hydrogen Fuel Cell Execution

Decommissioning: Plan and execute safe decommissioning of existing hydrogen infrastructure and fuel cell assets — isolation, purging/inerting, asset removal, site restoration, and disposition in accordance with Amazon standards and applicable safety codes
Infrastructure & fuel cell launch: Lead the launch of new hydrogen infrastructure and fuel cells per Amazon standards and processes — hydrogen storage and dispensing systems, hydrogen pads, piping, fueling infrastructure, and fuel cell power modules, from design review through installation, commissioning, and startup
Conversions: Manage conversions of existing sites to hydrogen fuel cell operation (or between configurations), coordinating the transition sequencing, infrastructure modifications, and cutover to minimize operational disruption
Coordinate with hydrogen fuel cell vendors and OEMs (e.g., Plug Power and equivalents) on equipment specifications, delivery schedules, and field support
Verify hydrogen systems meet Amazon specifications and applicable hydrogen safety and fire codes (e.g., NFPA 2, NFPA 55) throughout design, installation, and commissioning
Oversee fuel cell capacity planning, dispenser configuration, and integration with site power and operations

Procurement & Long-Lead Equipment Management

Own procurement for long-lead equipment across both domains — switchgear, generators, fuel cells, and hydrogen infrastructure components
Specify, order, track lead times, verify specifications, and coordinate delivery for critical-path equipment
Coordinate with manufacturers and vendors on custom configurations and delivery schedules
Escalate equipment delivery risks immediately when lead times threaten project schedules

Permitting & Regulatory

Own the permitting process for all sites — air permit applications for stationary generator installations and hydrogen-related permits and approvals
Prepare and submit permit applications across multiple jurisdictions and regulatory environments; track application status, agency review timelines, and approval milestones for each site
Navigate complex permitting scenarios including CEQA approvals, non-attainment areas, emission offset requirements, and hydrogen/fire code approvals
Coordinate with environmental and fire/life-safety consultants to develop applications, emission calculations, and hazard analyses
Maintain a permit tracking log with submission dates, agency contacts, expected approval dates, and required follow-ups
Proactively identify permitting risks and develop contingency plans to avoid schedule impacts; ensure all required emission and safety data is obtained from generator and fuel cell vendors

Project Execution & Delivery

Drive the end-to-end project lifecycle: feasibility, design, procurement, permitting, installation, commissioning, and handover
Develop and maintain detailed project schedules, budgets, risk registers, and status reports
Coordinate contractor mobilization, equipment procurement, and installation activities
Identify and resolve critical-path blockers with urgency; escalate issues proactively
Rely on extensive experience and judgment to plan and accomplish goals under compressed timelines

Stakeholder Management

Serve as the primary point of contact and single-threaded owner across all project stakeholders, aligning internal and external parties and holding each accountable to deliverables and timelines
Customer — Amazon Operations: partner with Amazon Operations (the internal customer) to understand site requirements, manage expectations, minimize operational disruption, and secure buy-in through launch and handover
General Contractor (GC): direct and hold the GC accountable for construction scope, schedule, RFIs, submittals, and field execution
Engineer of Record (EOR) & Architect of Record (AOR): coordinate design intent, drawing reviews, RFIs, and design changes; ensure the installed work conforms to the stamped design
Electrical Contractor (EC): coordinate electrical installation, terminations, testing, and energization activities and sequencing
Air permitting agencies & consultants: engage regulatory agencies and environmental consultants (e.g., Trinity) to secure and maintain air permits and keep applications on the critical path
Utility engagement — gas pipeline: drive utility coordination for natural gas pipeline connections, metering, pressure requirements, service applications, and interconnection timelines
Equipment vendors & OEMs: manage generator, switchgear, fuel cell, and hydrogen infrastructure vendors on specifications, lead times, and field support
Coordinate with Property/Construction Managers (PCMs) and Construction Managers at each site
Provide weekly status updates and monthly program reports to leadership

Site Launches, Commissioning & Energization

Travel to project sites during critical installation, commissioning, and decommissioning phases
Oversee equipment startup, testing, and acceptance procedures for both power and hydrogen systems
Ensure safe energization, hydrogen system startup, and transition to operations

Basic Qualifications

4+ years of program or project management experience
4+ years of defining and executing against program timeline & requirements experience
4+ years of driving end to end delivery, and communicating results to senior leadership experience
Experience using data and metrics to determine and drive improvements
Experience working cross functionally with tech and non-tech teams

Preferred Qualifications

4+ years of managing stakeholders in cross-functional project experience
4+ years of vendor management experience
Experience in stakeholder management, dealing with multiple stakeholders at varied levels of the organization
4+ years of leading large complex programs experience

Amazon is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of protected veteran status, disability, or other legally protected status.

Our inclusive culture empowers Amazonians to deliver the best results for our customers. If you have a disability and need a workplace accommodation or adjustment during the application and hiring process, including support for the interview or onboarding process, please visit https://amazon.jobs/content/en/how-we-hire/accommodations for more information. If the country/region you’re applying in isn’t listed, please contact your Recruiting Partner.

The base salary range for this position is listed below. Yo

Title:

State Role Title:
Prog Admin Specialist II

Up to $75,000

Dept of Veterans Services

RICHMOND (CITY)

Agency Website:
www.dvs.virginia.gov

Recruitment Type:
General Public - G

Job Duties

Calling Military Medicine Trailblazers, Workforce Innovators, and Pathway Builders!

What if a military medic or corpsman didn’t have to start over to build a civilian healthcare career?

The Virginia Department of Veterans Services is seeking a dynamic Military Medics and Corpsmen (MMAC) Program Lead to help turn military medical training and experience into meaningful pathways to civilian healthcare careers across the Commonwealth.

This is more than a program management role. You will bring together military talent, healthcare employers, colleges and universities, regulatory bodies, state agencies, and workforce partners to solve real barriers and build practical solutions. You will lead efforts to identify where military medical training can count toward academic credit, clinical requirements, credentials, and licensure—and help develop the referral systems and partnerships needed to make those pathways work.

You will lead the MMAC Program and its staff, strengthen career readiness and employment supports, expand clinical and educational pathways, and work with healthcare employers seeking to better recruit, train, and retain military-trained talent. You will also have an opportunity to contribute to legislative initiatives, regulatory discussions, and statewide work groups and help turn recommendations and policy changes into programs that work for veterans and Virginia’s healthcare workforce.

The ideal candidate is a builder, collaborator, and problem-solver who can move comfortably between strategy and implementation. Whether your background is in military medicine, healthcare, workforce development, education, credentialing, or program leadership, you should be excited by the opportunity to bring the right people to the table, challenge unnecessary barriers, and build pathways that recognize the value of military experience.

If you are ready to help Virginia rethink how military medical experience becomes civilian healthcare opportunity, we want to hear from you.

Key Responsibilities

Lead the MMAC Program and supervise assigned program staff.
Develop, implement, evaluate, and continuously improve MMAC career, credentialing, licensure, and education pathways.
Establish and maintain referral systems and partner networks supporting participants throughout the military-to-civilian healthcare transition.
Work alongside DHP boards, regulatory bodies, healthcare employers, educational institutions, workforce organizations, military partners, and other stakeholders to address pathway barriers.
Identify military educational and training equivalents applicable to healthcare education, certification, and licensure requirements.
Identify and expand clinical training opportunities for former military medical personnel.
Research and recommend opportunities to award academic credit for military medical education, training, and experience.
Provide career readiness, resource navigation, and employment-related support that helps participants understand and pursue appropriate civilian healthcare pathways.
Provide technical assistance to healthcare employers seeking to recruit, hire, train, and retain individuals with military healthcare experience.
Develop pathways across healthcare occupations and specialties, including nursing, behavioral health, dentistry, pharmacy, laboratory sciences, clinical specialties, and other areas where military medical experience may be applicable.
Support legislative, regulatory, policy, and work group initiatives related to military medical workforce pathways and assist with implementation of approved recommendations or statutory changes.
Maintain program data, performance measures, dashboards, partner engagement information, and reporting necessary to evaluate outcomes and inform program improvements.
Conduct presentations, outreach, stakeholder meetings, and other engagement activities to increase awareness and participation in MMAC.

Minimum Qualifications

Comprehensive knowledge of healthcare systems, workforce development, recruitment practices, and professional credentialing and licensure processes.
Knowledge of military healthcare occupations, training, and experience, including their civilian equivalents and pathways to healthcare employment, education, and professional advancement.
Demonstrated ability to develop, implement, and manage programs, including establishing strategic objectives, operational frameworks, performance measures, and continuous improvement strategies.
Demonstrated ability to develop and implement system requirements, standard operating procedures (SOPs), staff and partner expectations, and operational workflows to ensure program efficiency, compliance, and accountability.
Demonstrated experience in healthcare recruitment and job placement, including applicant screening, qualification assessments, employer referrals, job matching, and employment outcome tracking.
Ability to establish and maintain strategic partnerships with hospitals, healthcare systems, educational institutions, regulatory agencies, workforce development organizations, and other public and private stakeholders.
Ability to assess healthcare employer workforce needs and develop targeted recruitment, talent pipeline, and employment placement strategies for military-connected applicants.

new_jobs.title: Solution Consultant (External Program Manager) - Hybrid
new_jobs.description:
Brief Description

Job Type:
Direct hire

Company
: The name of our partner organization will be disclosed during the interview process. This is not a direct role with LaunchCode; it is a position through LaunchCode, working with one of our partner companies.

Disclaimer:
We are unable to provide work sponsorship for this role. We are unable to consider candidates for this role who have a current or future work sponsorship need (this includes those holding extended OPT Visas).

Our company partner is seeking a Solution Consultant, a product manager for their clients' businesses. You own the "what," the "why," and the business case. For each client in your portfolio, you learn their operation deeply enough to uncover the problems worth solving, quantify the value of solving them, and prioritize the opportunities with the strongest return. You maintain a living roadmap and backlog tied to measurable outcomes, then make clear, evidence-based recommendations that help clients confidently invest in the right work. You translate that direction for our development team with enough context and clarity that they can build it well. You are your clients' stakeholder, advocate, and champion for value.

You'll do this across several businesses at once, in industries you didn't know last quarter, for people who own the P&L. You recommend; the client decides. The job is won or lost on the quality of your thinking and your ability to make a case someone will act on. A recommendation nobody adopts is worth nothing here.

This is not order-taking. Clients rarely arrive with a well-formed problem statement. They arrive with symptoms, frustrations, spreadsheets held together with tape, and workarounds they stopped noticing years ago. Your job is to be curious enough to find what's actually underneath — and opinionated enough to tell them what to do about it.

Underneath all of it is shared understanding. Custom software development is almost certainly a new process for your client, and it asks them to make consequential decisions about something they can't see yet. Your job is to take them along — so that they, their users, and our developers are working from the same picture of the problem, the plan, and the trade-offs. We treat this as a first principle: where understanding is genuinely shared, results are predictable and expected. Where it quietly diverges, projects fail. Holding it together is continuous work, not a kickoff meeting.

What This Role Owns

Continuous discovery. Understand each client's business, goals, constraints, and context — and keep understanding them. Discovery isn't a phase you complete; it's a posture you hold for the life of the relationship.
Value identification and prioritization. Sift a large volume of information down to the handful of problems worth solving, and sequence them by the value they release.
Confident recommendation. Tell clients what you think they should do next, based on what you've learned, whether or not they asked.
Roadmap and backlog ownership. Maintain and evolve each client's roadmap and emerging backlog over time. Surface new opportunities before they're requested.
Shared understanding. Establish and maintain one picture of the problem, the plan, and the trade-offs across the client, their users, and our developers — and keep it current as all three change.
Measurable business outcomes. Connect every piece of work back to a business result — hours recovered, margin improved, risk reduced, revenue enabled.

What You'll Do

Get curious, and stay curious. Spend real time with clients — their people, their processes, their data, their numbers. Ask better questions than they've been asked before. Stick your nose where it wasn't invited. The best opportunities are almost always adjacent to the thing you were brought in to look at.
Learn industries fast. You won't know logistics, or medical device distribution, or specialty manufacturing before you walk in. You'll need to learn enough, quickly enough, to give advice a seasoned operator will respect.
Translate process into money. Read a P&L. Understand a client's KPIs and cost drivers. Be able to let the client see the real value of a proposed change.
Shape the solution. Work with our developers to pressure-test feasibility, approach, and effort. Know what's technically expensive and what's cheap, and steer clients accordingly. Know when the right answer is a small change to an existing system rather than a new build — or nothing at all.
Take the client along. Custom development is new territory for most of our clients. Teach them how it actually works — why we iterate, what a change costs and when, why their feedback is worth more in week two than week ten. Make the abstract visible with story maps, prototypes, and demos. Write things down. And test for real understanding rather than accepting the polite nod, because the gap you don't find now is the one that surfaces at delivery.
Get the work built. Translate direction into well-formed epics and stories with clear context, acceptance criteria, and business rationale. Stay with the work through the build so intent doesn't get lost between the conversation and the code.
Advocate internally. Represent your clients in planning, scoping, and prioritization discussions. Make sure what we deliver is what matters to them.
Raise the bar. If you come in with more consulting and business maturity than the room, we want you to use it. This seat has room to grow into one that elevates the whole consulting team.

What You Need To Bring

The mechanics of the role — our discovery process, story mapping, backlog grooming, our tooling — are learnable, and we don't expect them on day one. These aren't, and they're what we'll hire on:

Deep curiosity. Not professional interest — actual curiosity about how businesses work and why people do things the way they do.
Analytical instinct for value. Given a mess of information, you find the thread that matters. You're comfortable being decisive about what's not worth doing.
Business acumen. Operations, financial concepts, KPIs, process improvement, organizational dynamics. You think like an operator, not a requirements gatherer.
Financial literacy. Enough comfort with financial statements and business metrics to reason about margin, cost, and payback without hedging.
A drive for shared understanding. You assume you've been misunderstood until you've confirmed otherwise, and you can tell the difference between agreement and a nod.
The confidence to challenge. You'll tell a client their process is the problem, that the feature they asked for is a bad idea, or that they're the bottleneck — with enough care that they thank you for it.
The ability to make a case. You don't have authority here. Your leverage is a well-built argument, backed by numbers the client can check, delivered to someone who has other priorities.
Client empathy. You can deliver a hard message because people trust that you're on their side.
Adaptability. New industry, new client, new vocabulary, every few months. You find that energizing rather than exhausting.
A continuous learning mindset. The half-life of what you know here is short.

Qualifications

A background in client-facing consulting, solution consulting, business analysis, or product management / product ownership — ideally in a services or agency environment. We're open on level; we care more about what you can do than how long you've been doing it.
A track record of translating business needs into requirements a technical team could actually build from
Experience facilitating discovery sessions and workshops with stakeholders from frontline users to executives
Strong written communication — much of your influence will happen in documents and summaries
Technical fluency enough to reason credibly about databases, integrations, APIs, and system boundaries — and to earn developers' respect. You don't need to write production code.

Helpful, Not Required

Exposure to FileMaker, low-code platforms, or custom business application development
Integration experience across CRMs, ERPs, and accounting systems
Background in one of our core verticals (manufacturing, logistics, professional services, healthcare)
Familiarity with EOS or a similar operating framework

How We'll Measure Success

First 90 days: You know our delivery model, our tooling, and our team. You've shadowed active engagements and taken primary ownership of at least one client relationship.
First 6 months: You're running discovery independently. Every client in your portfolio has a maintained roadmap, and nothing we deliver surprises them. Your clients can articulate the value of the work in flight, and your development team rarely comes back to you for missing context.
First 12 months: Your accounts are growing because the work is delivering measurable results, and clients are bringing you problems earlier — before they've decided what the answer is.

Salt Lake County is seeking a Data and Analytics Project Manager to lead the planning and coordination efforts to implement the cross-sector data and technology efforts outlined in recommendations 22-25 of its Behavioral Health and Justice Action Plan (https//www.saltlakecounty.gov/mayor/action-plan/). The Plan is a ten-year, multi-faceted effort to transform how our systems address behavioral health, criminal justice and homelessness. This work reflects a rare alignment of internal momentum and external stakeholder support around a comprehensive, coordinated approach. Reporting to the Human Services Executive Office and in partnership with the County Information Technology division, the Office of Criminal Justice and Homelessness Reform as well as other county agencies (including elected officials), this position will manage developing the data and technology strategy, including data governance, integration and standardization across behavioral health, jail, courts, law enforcement, pretrial and parole, prosecution and indigent defense agencies. This role will coordinate data-sharing across internal teams and external partners, including providers, the State of Utah, and municipalities, ensuring data are accurate, accessible, and actionable. It will also work closely with program data analysts to improve data utilization and reporting to improve care coordination for individuals as well as to evaluate program outcomes. This position will not lead the technical implementation of the integration technology infrastructure but will partner with technology staff to identify and implement solutions.

This role requires strong organizational and people skills, attention to detail, ability to work in evolving circumstances, and the ability to communicate effectively with state, county and municipal leaders as well as a broad spectrum of stakeholders. A strong understanding of behavioral health and justice systems is a big plus. Funding for this position has been approved for 5 years.

Job Summary

Leads the development and implementation of Salt Lake County’s cross-system data strategy to support behavioral health and justice system transformation. Collaborates with County’s IT, data privacy, and agency data teams to establish enterprise data governance frameworks, enable secure and effective data sharing across agencies, and implement an integrated data system to support performance measurement and decision making for the Behavioral Health and Justice Action Plan.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in public or business administration, data science, information systems, criminal justice, or a related field, plus five (5) years of progressively responsible experience, including three (3) years of project management experience involving data and/or information technology efforts or other complex projects; OR an equivalent combination of education and experience.

Due to the nature of this position, the successful applicant must pass a required background check through fingerprinting and enrollment in the continuous RAP Back (Record of Arrest and Prosecution Back) program in accordance with current County Human Resources policy requirements.

Essential Functions

Leads collaborative efforts to design, develop, coordinate, and implement an integrated cross-agency data infrastructure required to support the County’s Behavioral Health and Justice Reform initiatives.
Leads efforts to establish a long-term vision for data integration and ensures alignment with County priorities, policy goals, and system-wide outcomes.
Serves as the County lead for cross-agency behavioral health and criminal justice data collaboration, bringing together departments, state agencies, courts, law enforcement, service providers, and other partners to align data-sharing practices and system objectives.
Facilitates and leads the cross-agency Data and Analytics Workgroup and other related meetings by establishing agendas, facilitating meaningful participation, tracking action items and ensuring follow-up related to data integration, system performance, and technology implementation.
Coordinates with County IT and Data Privacy teams to develop and manage data governance structures, including policies, MOUs, procedures, and protocols related to data sharing, privacy, and data security, and to ensure compliance with federal, state, and local laws and regulations regarding data privacy, confidentiality, and information security.
Supports the County’s efforts to evaluate, procure, implement, and maintain technology solutions that enable an integrated data system.

Methods for integrating and managing data across multiple systems and organizations

OVERVIEW:

This is an opportunity for a rewarding and career-enhancing experience working on the tropical island of Guam, located between Hawaii and the Philippines in the western North Pacific Ocean. Along with miles of pristine sandy beaches, coral reefs, beautiful mountains and valleys, Guam has 4,000 years of history ranging from the site of Magellan’s landing to Spanish Forts and WWII battle sites. Take advantage of the wonders of Guam, as well as explore Japan, Thailand, the Philippines, and many other exotic locations within Southeast Asia, most just a short direct flight away.

This position will lead the on-site construction oversight team, providing Construction Management Agency (CMa) services for the construction of a large and complex headquarters project. The CMa team will provide turnkey services to the client from the field as well as be supported by reach back resources as necessary.

EXPERIENCE QUALIFICATION:

MBP is seeking adventurous leaders in the construction industry who are looking to gain overseas experience, growth opportunities, and work on significant and meaningful projects in support of our national security. For this position, we seek a candidate with 15 or more years of experience in construction/project management to support MBP’s growth and advancement in the Guam and Indo-Pacific region. The candidate should exhibit evidence of progressive career development and demonstrated expertise in construction management, project management, engineering design, or related fields, ideally including oversight of successful projects within the Federal sector.

MAIN DUTIES:

Provide owner representation for medium—to large construction projects ($100 - $500 million) from conception to completion. This position will be part of an on-site team supporting the work and overall responsibilities, including managing cost, schedule, and quality on behalf of the client/owner. Typical duties include:
Actively engage with the clients and project stakeholders to proactively manage risks and resolve issues.
Monitors and manages client project budgets.
Review and/or oversee the review of project schedules, submittals, RFIs, daily reports, payment applications, change proposals, and other typical construction activities. Ensure items are complete, reasonable, and addressed in a timely manner.
Oversee the implementation of a construction quality management process to verify that the work performed is in compliance with contract requirements. Record and track issues until resolution.
Participate and/or lead progress meetings with client and other senior stakeholder personnel.
Coordinate and oversee other third-party owner contractors.
Monitor and verify completion of closeout requirements, including owner training, operations and maintenance manuals, warranties, and stock materials.

ADDITIONAL DUTIES:

Participation in company initiatives.
Participate in professional association meetings.
Stay abreast of new trends and innovations.
Mentor and facilitate the imparting of technical knowledge to staff including the transfer of technical knowledge to those with less experience.
As necessary, assist in interviewing and recommendation of candidates to fill vacancies and build capabilities within the workforce.

EDUCATION/KNOWLEDGE:

B.S. in industry-related field, advanced degree preferred. Relevant work experience or other education may be considered in lieu of a degree.
Professional registration, other specific industry-related certification, or advanced specialized technical knowledge.
Detailed knowledge of construction, principles of construction management, commissioning, and/or project controls, with specialized knowledge in one or more of MBP’s services. Knowledge and demonstrated experience in project management techniques, including budgeting, leadership, training, and business develoment.
Past experience working on Federal projects preferred.

SKILLS AND ABILITIES:

Capable of managing a large, complex project from conception to completion.
Ability to establish positive and productive working relationships with peer leaders, superiors, and subordinates.
Ability to develop and maintain effective working relationships with those contacted in the course of the work and effectively act as a representative of the Owner/Client.
Ability to analyze problems, identify alternative solutions, and consequences of proposed actions and implement recommendations in support of goals.
Skilled at preparing clear, concise, and accurate reports and presentations.
Skilled at crisis management and problem resolution.
Must have computer skills and be proficient in the use of Microsoft Office applications, email, Internet navigation, web-based tools and other specialized equipment.

Project Manager

You are a resourceful, knowledgeable, and self-motivated security professional who thrives in a collaborative and supportive environment.

Strong self-awareness of strengths and development areas with a curiosity and appetite for change and innovation

Strong analytical skills with critical thinking driven by data

Ability to evaluate outputs rigorously to ensure consistent excellence in delivery

Ability to think proactively about the future of the business and relate current business activities to desired outcomes

POSITION RESPONSIBILITIES

The essential duties and responsibilities include, but are not limited to the following:

Project Management

Identify project schedule, scope parameters, and oversee security design and implementation per client design requirements and standards.
Manage early project initiation activities and develop project security scope, schedule, critical deliverables, and requirements.
Manage scheduling, status, and tracking of critical project tasks, issues, and deliverables.

Design

Redline documentation with corrections and log issues, as required.

Collaborate

Attend regular project design, project management, Owner/Architect/Contractor (OAC), and construction meetings.
Manage site activation activities for physical security amongst project parties and stakeholders to drive schedule, quality, and cost.
Coordinate with ZBeta design resources to develop the complete scope of work documents for security systems procurement and installation.

Documentation

Produce project status and issues reports and meet with client stakeholders weekly to review and resolve high-priority project issues.
Log all instances of issue resolutions that constitute exceptions to the published client security requirements to facilitate effective requirements exceptions reporting and/or requirement document updates.

Quality Control

Conduct on-site inspections during construction and installation and final acceptance testing of completed systems installation.
Manage project lessons learned, site metrics evaluation, and contractor performance evaluations.
Review all security system design documentation produced by the system designer for compliance with published security requirements, technical standards, and installation standards.
Oversee the delivery of all shop drawings and close-out documentation required from the integrator/contractor.

3+ years of project management experience, preferably in consulting with external clients on program development initiatives, and aggressively scheduled design and delivery projects

Bachelor’s degree or equivalent work experience

Working familiarity with low-voltage and physical security technology and design concepts

Demonstrated ability to identify critical path activities, prioritize tasks and deliverables, and realize consistent progress

Competitive salary based on job-related skills, experience, and qualifications

new_jobs.title: Sr. Construction Program Manager, Worldwide Grocery Stores - Growth & Development
new_jobs.description:
Description

Amazon's Worldwide Grocery Stores, Growth & Development team is seeking a Sr. Construction Program Manager, a leader who combines deep construction industry expertise with the strategic vision and operational rigor needed to build scalable programs from the ground up. This is a program-focused role, not a Construction Project Manager position. You'll design governance frameworks, formalize what doesn't exist, fix what's broken at a systemic level, and equip hundreds of team members to do their jobs more effectively through disciplined Procore adoption, structured training, and scalable SOPs.

As our portfolio scales, information must flow end-to-end with minimal manual intervention, and every team member from Design to Construction Project Managers to Store Operations must be appropriately equipped to operate within governed, consistent processes. You will own that outcome - not by managing individual projects, but by designing, governing, and continuously improving the systems, standards, and tools that construction teams operate within so that our team can successfully execute individual project outcomes.

Key job responsibilities

Responsibilities

This role spans construction program strategy, platform governance, and organizational enablement across a portfolio of more than 600 active pipeline projects and growing. Core responsibilities include:

Develop and govern company policy, construction standards, and the Whole Foods Market (WFM) standard construction specification book.
Own end-to-end Procore process governance for execution teams (RFI, Submittals, Bidding Tool, and PCO/CCO workflows) and ensure information flows seamlessly across the construction lifecycle.
Advocate for system enhancements, integrations, and functionality improvements that drive scalability as the portfolio grows.
Govern value engineering review processes and cost governance frameworks across the construction portfolio.
Partner with Strategic Category Management and Vendor Management on GC performance assessment and scorecard frameworks.
Develop and govern permitting and entitlements coordination frameworks across multiple jurisdictions.
Define milestone frameworks and scheduling standards that Construction Operations Groups operate within.
Build and deliver role-based training curricula, SOP libraries, and change management programs for Procore and Coupa adoption.
Identify AI and automation opportunities within construction workflows and develop roadmaps in partnership with the LSA Product Management team.

A day in the life

No two days look exactly the same. You start your morning reviewing Procore compliance dashboards, flagging a pattern in stalled submittals (a process gap, not a project problem) for leadership. Mid-morning, you're presenting a business case for a Bidding Tool integration to a Procore Steering Committee. After lunch, you're facilitating cross-functional alignment across Pipeline, Indirect Procurement, and Construction teams. Late afternoon, you're delivering a Procore onboarding session using a curriculum you built. By end of week, you've advanced two SOPs, submitted enhancement requests, and documented a training gap to close next quarter.

About The Team

Amazon's Worldwide Retail Grocery Development (WWRGD) team manages the full lifecycle of Amazon and Whole Foods Market grocery retail and industrial facilities — from pre-lease due diligence through construction delivery, facilities maintenance, and decommissioning. With more than 600 active sites, 100+ active pipeline locations, and a portfolio scaling toward 2,000+ active projects, we operate at the intersection of construction, technology, and organizational scale. Our mission is to deliver best-in-class facilities faster, at best value, and with greater consistency across every site we build and maintain.

Basic Qualifications

Bachelor's degree
7+ years of project management, real estate development, architecture/design experience
Experience in construction, or experience developing MOPs and SWMS for planned works
Demonstrated Procore expertise across RFI, Submittals, Bidding, Change Management, and PCO/CCO financial workflow modules
Experience developing and governing permitting, entitlements, and regulatory compliance frameworks across multiple jurisdictions
Proficiency in data analysis and reporting with ability to translate construction program data into executive-facing insights (PowerBI or equivalent)

Preferred Qualifications

Experience developing and implementing training programs
Project Management Professional (PMP) certification, or experience in project, program or product management with focus on technical education programs
Experience using managed ML/AI solutions
Experience in grocery retail, food service, or temperature-controlled facility construction environments

Amazon is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of protected veteran status, disability, or other legally protected status.

Our inclusive culture empowers Amazonians to deliver the best results for our customers. If you have a disability and need a workplace accommodation or adjustment during the application and hiring process, including support for the interview or onboarding process, please visit https://amazon.jobs/content/en/how-we-hire/accommodations for more information. If the country/region you’re applying in isn’t listed, please contact your Recruiting Partner.

The base salary range for this position is listed below. Your Amazon package will include sign-on payments and restricted stock units (RSUs). Final compensation will be determined based on factors including experience, qualifications, and location. Amazon also offers comprehensive benefits including health insurance (medical, dental, vision, prescription, Basic Life & AD&D insurance and option for Supplemental life plans, EAP, Mental Health Support, Medical Advice Line, Flexible Spending Accounts, Adoption and Surrogacy Reimbursement coverage), 401(k) matching, paid time off, and parental leave. Learn more about our benefits at https://amazon.jobs/en/benefits.

Description

Amazon's Worldwide Grocery Stores, Growth & Development team is seeking a Sr. Construction Program Manager, a leader who combines deep construction industry expertise with the strategic vision and operational rigor needed to build scalable programs from the ground up. This is a program-focused role, not a Construction Project Manager position. You'll design governance frameworks, formalize what doesn't exist, fix what's broken at a systemic level, and equip hundreds of team members to do their jobs more effectively through disciplined Procore adoption, structured training, and scalable SOPs.

As our portfolio scales, information must flow end-to-end with minimal manual intervention, and every team member from Design to Construction Project Managers to Store Operations must be appropriately equipped to operate within governed, consistent processes. You will own that outcome - not by managing individual projects, but by designing, governing, and continuously improving the systems, standards, and tools that construction teams operate within so that our team can successfully execute individual project outcomes.

Key job responsibilities

Responsibilities

This role spans construction program strategy, platform governance, and organizational enablement across a portfolio of more than 600 active pipeline projects and growing. Core responsibilities include:

Develop and govern company policy, construction standards, and the Whole Foods Market (WFM) standard construction specification book.
Own end-to-end Procore process governance for execution teams (RFI, Submittals, Bidding Tool, and PCO/CCO workflows) and ensure information flows seamlessly across the construction lifecycle.
Advocate for system enhancements, integrations, and functionality improvements that drive scalability as the portfolio grows.
Govern value engineering review processes and cost governance frameworks across the construction portfolio.
Partner with Strategic Category Management and Vendor Management on GC performance assessment and scorecard frameworks.
Develop and govern permitting and entitlements coordination frameworks across multiple jurisdictions.
Define milestone frameworks and scheduling standards that Construction Operations Groups operate within.
Build and deliver role-based training curricula, SOP libraries, and change management programs for Procore and Coupa adoption.
Identify AI and automation opportunities within construction workflows and develop roadmaps in partnership with the LSA Product Management team.

A day in the life

No two days look exactly the same. You start your morning reviewing Procore compliance dashboards, flagging a pattern in stalled submittals (a process gap, not a project problem) for leadership. Mid-morning, you're presenting a business case for a Bidding Tool integration to a Procore Steering Committee. After lunch, you're facilitating cross-functional alignment across Pipeline, Indirect Procurement, and Construction teams. Late afternoon, you're delivering a Procore onboarding session using a curriculum you built. By end of week, you've advanced two SOPs, submitted enhancement requests, and documented a training gap to close next quarter.

About The Team

Amazon's Worldwide Retail Grocery Development (WWRGD) team manages the full lifecycle of Amazon and Whole Foods Market grocery retail and industrial facilities — from pre-lease due diligence through construction delivery, facilities maintenance, and decommissioning. With more than 600 active sites, 100+ active pipeline locations, and a portfolio scaling toward 2,000+ active projects, we operate at the intersection of construction, technology, and organizational scale. Our mission is to deliver best-in-class facilities faster, at best value, and with greater consistency across every site we build and maintain.

7+ years of project management, real estate development, architecture/design experience
Experience in construction, or experience developing MOPs and SWMS for planned works
Demonstrated Procore expertise across RFI, Submittals, Bidding, Change Management, and PCO/CCO financial workflow modules
Experience developing and governing permitting, entitlements, and regulatory compliance frameworks across multiple jurisdictions
Proficiency in data analysis and reporting with ability to translate construction program data into executive-facing insights (PowerBI or equivalent)

Role Title:
Business Analyst (Arabic Language) Remote
Role Type:
Full-time
Location:
Remote

Role Overview:

We are looking for candidates with strong analytical and English comprehension skills. The ideal candidate should have the ability to read, summarize, and break down large content into smaller logical blocks, conduct research online, validate claims made in the content through online research, and work with the LLM (Large Language Models) to solve puzzles!

Your role is critical in helping fine-tune and improve large language models (like gpt), and will make you an expert on how to leverage AI to be a better analyst. This is your chance to future-proof your career in an AI-first world!

What does day-to-day look like:

You would spend time answering a variety of interesting analytical questions and creating scenarios that can train the LLM models to get better. Here are a couple of examples which models might get wrong and you would have to give the correct answer and explanation to enable the models to learn:

1. Based on a given distribution of sales by month across locations, could you analyze which location has grown the most? (Hint: what time period should we look at? should we account for sudden variability at the beginning?)
2. In a small town, there are four distinct neighborhoods: Oak, Pine, Maple, and Elm. A postman is assigned to deliver mail and can only deliver to two neighborhoods in one day, with certain rules (e.g. Oak is always visited before Pine). If he delivers to Oak and Elm on the first day, which neighborhoods does the carrier deliver to on the second day?
Note: No other prior specialized domain experience is needed.

Requirements:

1. Multilingual capabilities are mandatory. (English and Arabic)
2. Analytical Skills: Good research and analytical skills
3. Feedback Skills: Ability to provide constructive feedback and detailed annotations.
4. Creative Thinking: Creative and lateral thinking abilities.
5. Communication: Excellent communication and collaboration skills.
6. Independence: Self-motivated and able to work independently in a remote setting.
7. Commitment: Ability to commit to 40 hours per week for the contract duration overlapping US hours.
8. Technical Setup: Desktop/Laptop set up with a good internet connection.

Preferred Qualifications:

1. Bachelors degree or undergraduate in Engineering, Literature, Journalism, Communications, Arts, Statistics, or a related field. We are open to candidates who do not have a Bachelor's degree but have experience in the area.
2. Experience writing professionally (business analysts, research analyst, copywriter, journalist, technical writer, editor, translator, etc.)
3. Understanding of Excel and Google Suite.
4. Proficiency in Data interpretation, Logical reasoning and Basic arithmetic is highly desirable.

Benefits:

1. Competitive compensation based on experience and expertise.
2. Flexible working hours and remote work environment.
3. Opportunity to work on cutting-edge AI projects with leading LLM companies.
